title: Multi-state Protein Sequence Design with DynamicMPNN
claim: Many proteins switch between conformations, so we train one model on whole conformational ensembles and evaluate it with a structure-prediction loop.
layout: 2 stacked panels; top gallery of state pairs, bottom left-to-right pipeline with dashed evaluation loop
description: Panel (a), at the top, shows three pairs of protein ribbon structures in light blue. Each pair is joined by an equilibrium arrow and labeled Transporter, Metamorphic or Hinge. Panel (b) is a left-to-right schematic. A conformational ensemble of two states, one teal and one red, with gray interaction partners, goes through backbone feature extraction. The features enter a stacked Multi-State GNN Encoder box. The encoder output goes to a pool block, then an Auto-Regressive Sequence Decoder, then a predicted sequence 'QSWYLL...'. Dashed teal, red and gray lines form the evaluation loop. They feed the target structures and the predicted sequence into three AF3 boxes, along with a gray decoy structure. The AF3 outputs lead to Structural Self-Consistency Scores (RMSD, pLDDT, TM-Score) and then to Normalized Scores. Color codes the conformational states.
caption: DynamicMPNN for multi-state protein design. (a) Examples of proteins with multiple conformational states: transporters in closed and open states (PDB: 6NC7, 6NC9), metamorphic protein with alternative folds (PDB: 4QHH, 4QHF) and hinges showing domain movement (PDB: 5D0W, 1CFC). (b) Schematic of DynamicMPNN, an inverse folding model trained to generate protein sequences with multiple conformational states. Conformations are encoded with their respective chemical environments (i.e. interaction partners shown in gray). Solid lines show the flow of information in the model, while dashed lines show the evaluation pipeline using AlphaFold 3 (AF3); employing target structures as templates during inference and measuring the deviations between predicted and target structures, with decoy structures serving as negative controls.
abstract: Structural biology has long been dominated by the one sequence, one structure, one function paradigm, yet many critical biological processes—from enzyme catalysis to membrane transport—depend on proteins that adopt multiple conformational states. Existing multi-state design approaches rely on post-hoc aggregation of single-state predictions, achieving poor experimental success rates compared to single-state design. We introduce DynamicMPNN, an inverse folding model explicitly trained to generate sequences compatible with multiple conformations through joint learning across conformational ensembles. Trained on 46,033 conformational pairs covering 75% of CATH superfamilies and evaluated using Alphafold 3, DynamicMPNN outperforms ProteinMPNN by up to 31% on decoy-normalized RMSD and by 12% on sequence recovery across our challenging multi-state protein benchmark.
